intro: Before you rises the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, built in 353 - 350 BC. It is one of the Seven Wonders, and the building every mausoleum is named after: the tomb that Artemisia, his sister and wife, raised for Mausolus, satrap of Caria. Let your eye climb it stage by stage: a tall podium, thirty-six columns, a stepped pyramid, and on the summit a four-horse chariot.
spot-1: Now you are looking at the podium, 18.5 metres high and built in three tiers. The friezes once wrapped around these tiers, carrying the eye upward.
spot-2: Now look at the lions. Twenty lion statues were found round the podium, and every one of them faces outwards, as if keeping watch over the tomb.
spot-3: Your gaze moves up to the colonnade: thirty-six Ionic columns, nine by eleven, with statues standing in the spaces between them.
spot-4: Above the columns rises the pyramid, a roof climbing seven metres in twenty-four steps.
spot-5: And at the very top, the quadriga: the marble chariot crowning the whole monument, with four horses, Mausolus and Artemisia. One of the horses' heads is now in London.
uncertainty: Finally, what this model does not know. The foundation dimensions, the heights of the podium, pyramid and quadriga, and the column and step counts come from the German Wikipedia; the lion count comes from the English one. Because the building was quarried into Bodrum Castle in the 15th century, everything else is interpretation, drawn from Pliny's description and the excavated foundation. The three tiers of the podium, the 12 m column height, the shape of the cella, the summit platform and the pose of the quadriga are proportion, not measurement. The three relief friezes round the podium, showing Amazons, centaurs and a chariot race, are absent, as are most of the four hundred statues; the figures between the columns and the lions are there simply to show the arrangement.
